episode_title: How do we turn data centers into the industry of choice with Kaitlin Schaberg

real_qa.q: How has power capacity demand in data centers evolved from kilowatts to gigawatts since the early 2010s?
real_qa.r: When Kaitlin Schaberg first joined QTS, deals were typically in the 200-250 kilowatt range. Today, deals are being done at the gigawatt level, which is a thousand times larger than megawatts. This scale shift reflects the massive growth in infrastructure needed to support new technologies like AI, with megawatt-level deals now being the minimum for companies to remain competitive.
real_qa.requete: data center power capacity kilowatts to gigawatts evolution

real_qa.q: What infrastructure benefits do data centers provide to local communities beyond just energy consumption?
real_qa.r: Data centers provide community infrastructure foundations by bringing power substations and new power lines to areas that previously lacked them, which then catalyzes fiber and water utility development. This creates opportunities for retail, residential, and other development in the region. DC Blocks considers community engagement a foundational value and runs sustainability programs including tree planting, murals, and partnerships with municipalities for parks and school contributions.
real_qa.requete: data center community infrastructure benefits local development

real_qa.q: Why is the data center industry becoming more attractive to younger professionals due to AI visibility?
real_qa.r: Data centers are transitioning from an overlooked 'unsexy' industry to a mainstream topic due to AI's prominence. With AI requiring massive backend infrastructure, data centers are now recognized as the backbone of innovation. This increased visibility in mainstream news and conversations has created new college programs and internship opportunities that didn't exist before, making the industry more accessible and appealing to young professionals.
real_qa.requete: data center industry AI visibility younger professionals careers

real_qa.q: What diverse career paths does the data center industry offer for professionals from different educational backgrounds?
real_qa.r: The data center industry uniquely allows professionals with backgrounds in construction management, engineering, architecture, and real estate to converge into data center roles. Unlike other industries, someone can enter from any of these disciplines and find pathways through design, construction, real estate, or operations, with exposure to customers' businesses and partner organizations throughout the delivery process.
real_qa.requete: data center career paths construction engineering architecture real estate

real_qa.q: How does AI adoption drive future power and cooling demands in global data centers?
real_qa.r: AI workloads will operate primarily in the gigawatt power space rather than the megawatt space, requiring significant innovation in power and cooling efficiency. Schaberg notes there will be numerous new companies created around AI and existing industries will use AI to support their operations, creating a complex challenge for data centers and their partners to navigate the right efficiency path forward.
real_qa.requete: AI gigawatt power cooling data center efficiency future

guest.bio_context: Kaitlin Schaberg is a Stanford University graduate with over seven years of experience in the data center industry. She began her career at QTS, one of the top three global data center companies, where she held roles spanning finance, operations, construction, and sales before joining DC Blocks. She was recently included in Data Center Magazine's Top 100 Industry Women list.

real_quote: If you're not sure what you want to do, but you want to be in tech, keep some of these things in mind, because there are pathways that you probably don't even know about yet.
key_stats: 200-250 kilowatts: typical power capacity for deals when Schaberg joined QTS
Gigawatt level: current scale of major data center deals today
Seven to eight years: Schaberg's tenure in the data center industry
Data Center Magazine's Top 100 Industry Women list: first year of publication when Schaberg was included
Thousand times larger: the scale multiplier from kilowatts to megawatts to gigawatts
